name: Madeira
description: Run x86-64 Windows PC games on jailed iOS via FEX-Emu + Wine + DXMT
readmeHtml:
Madeira runs Windows PC games on an iPhone, with no jailbreak. Games run as they are, unmodified, inside a single iOS app.

Note

Madeira is an active research project. Many games start and some play well, but performance and compatibility vary from game to game, and things change quickly. Expect rough edges.

How it works

Layer What it does
FEX-Emu Translates the game's x86 and x86-64 code to ARM64 as it runs.
Wine 11.4 Provides Windows. It is built for ARM64EC, so Wine itself runs natively and only the game's own code is translated. 32-bit games run through WoW64.
DXMT Draws Direct3D 9, 10 and 11 with Metal.
madeira-d3d12 Madeira's own Direct3D 12 implementation on Metal, converting DXIL shaders at run time with Apple's Metal Shader Converter.

iOS apps cannot start other programs, so everything runs in one process: even Wine's server runs as a thread instead of a separate program.

Features

  • Game library with artwork, search and a Windows desktop session.
  • Steam: sign in, browse the games you own, install and update them, and start them through Valve's own Windows Steam client (Madeira Dock).
  • Steam Cloud saves: saves sync with Steam Cloud when Madeira starts and before a game starts, and Upload saves and close Madeira in the game menu sends them when you stop playing. Saves that changed on both sides are never overwritten without asking, and anything a sync replaces is backed up.
  • Controllers: Bluetooth controllers through XInput, plus customisable on-screen touch controls.
  • Keyboard, mouse and trackpad passed through to games as real input.
  • Video and audio for cutscenes and music, through FFmpeg, VideoToolbox and AudioToolbox.

Requirements

  • An iPhone on iOS 26 or later, the only version Madeira currently runs on reliably. Development happens on recent Pro iPhones.
  • JIT, which iOS only allows while a debugger is attached. Madeira can use StikDebug or its built-in StikJIT helper. On iOS 27 the built-in helper can pair the iPhone itself, without a computer.
  • An Apple ID to sideload the app. A free account works; its signing expires after 7 days, so the app needs refreshing weekly. Your games and saves are kept across reinstalls.

Because JIT needs a debugger, Madeira cannot be offered on the App Store.

Installing

  1. Download the IPA from the latest release.
  2. Sideload it with your own Apple ID using SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or a similar tool.
  3. Open Madeira and enable JIT. Automatic mode uses StikDebug when installed, otherwise it guides you through the built-in setup; see JIT setup.
  4. In Settings, check that JIT and Memory+ both show a green check: Madeira then says Ready to play.

Some 64-bit games need Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime, which is not included (see Licensing).

Building from source

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/willfaust/Madeira.git

FEX, wine, dxmt and madeira-dock are submodules that point at Madeira's own forks; upstream checkouts will not build here. The build has several parts (the Wine unix libraries, the ARM64EC Windows modules, FEX, DXMT and the app) and some inputs that are not in the repository, such as the toolchains. docs/BUILDING.md walks through all of it.

Repository layout

Path Contents
app/ The iOS app: SwiftUI front end, Wine bridge and bundled resources
wine/, FEX/, dxmt/, madeira-dock/ Madeira's forks and the Steam client launcher (submodules)
madeira-d3d12/ The native Direct3D 12 runtime
build/ Build scripts and iOS-side sources, one folder per component
tests/ Host checks and x86, x86-64 and DXMT test programs
tools/ Helper scripts
docs/ Documentation
research/ Experiments that are not part of the app

Documentation

Topic Document
Building from a clean checkout docs/BUILDING.md
StikDebug and built-in JIT setup docs/JIT.md
The game library docs/LIBRARY.md
Steam sign-in, library and downloads docs/STEAM_SIGNIN.md, docs/STEAM_LIBRARY.md
Steam Cloud saves docs/STEAM_CLOUD.md
Madeira Dock (the Steam client) docs/MADEIRA_DOCK.md
32-bit games (WoW64) docs/WOW64.md
Controllers and touch controls docs/CONTROLLERS.md
Keyboard, mouse and trackpad docs/KEYBOARD_MOUSE.md
Audio and video docs/MEDIA.md
Licensing in detail docs/LICENSING.md

Licensing

Madeira is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later (LICENSE) with the Madeira Converter Exception (LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md), an additional permission that allows it to work with Apple's Metal Shader Converter.

The projects it builds on keep their own licenses upstream, but Madeira's forks are not all licensed the same way as their upstreams:

Component License
Wine fork LGPL-2.1-or-later, like upstream Wine
FEX-Emu fork, DXMT fork Upstream code stays MIT; Madeira's changes are GPL-3.0-or-later with the exception
rpmalloc fork Upstream code stays 0BSD; Madeira's changes are GPL-3.0-or-later with the exception
Madeira Dock GPL-3.0-or-later with the exception

Anything obtained earlier under a permissive license stays available under it. Per-component details, including GnuTLS, Nettle, GMP, FFmpeg and LLVM, are in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md; the license texts are in LICENSES/.

Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not distributed with Madeira. To build with them, supply them yourself as described in tools/fetch-vcruntime.md.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome under GPL-3.0-or-later; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

Madeira's forks contain a lot of AI-assisted work. FEX-Emu does not accept AI-generated code, so please do not send changes from these forks upstream to FEX-Emu, and check each upstream project's contribution policy before proposing anything to it.

Credits

  • Will Faust (@willfaust): created Madeira
  • Nick (@125hz): 32-bit game support, the game library and Madeira Dock
  • Jfishin (@Jfishin): the original native Steam sign-in, library and downloads
  • Jesse (@JesseLovelace): Steam Cloud saves, faster game launches, and fixes that let more games run
  • Dan Perks (@danperks): in-app JIT without StikDebug, and pairing without a computer
  • bahacan16 (@bahacan16): Direct3D 12 and DXMT fixes, game launcher windows, per-game settings, PlayStation controllers, and save backups
  • spitefulowl (@spitefulowl): Wine and FEX runtime fixes, DXMT texture and memory fixes, audio, the swap tier, and library launch options
  • meshoklv (@meshoklv): controller fixes for games that ship their own XInput or need focus, touch taps that stay off the mouse, and a crash-guard fix

Madeira is built on Wine, FEX-Emu, DXMT by Feifan He (3Shain) with the Direct3D 9 frontend by David Acevedo (dacevedo12), rpmalloc by Mattias Jansson, StikDebug, StikJIT and idevice for enabling JIT. Thank you to everyone who contributes to them.

Join the community on Discord

releases.name: Madeira 0.1.3
releases.body:
### New
- **In-app JIT: no StikDebug needed.** Madeira can enable JIT by itself through a bundled helper built on StikJIT. On iOS 27 it pairs with the iPhone it runs on: in Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode, tap **Pair with Madeira** and enter the PIN Madeira shows. No computer needed. On iOS 26, import a pairing file instead. The pairing is kept in the Keychain. StikDebug still works. (#127)
- **Play turns JIT on for you.** If JIT is off, Play enables it and then starts the game. The button reads **Starting JIT** meanwhile.
- **Madeira JIT shortcut (iOS 27, optional).** LocalDevVPN's loopback does not work over cellular data. The shortcut connects LocalDevVPN, turns Cellular Data off when there is no Wi-Fi, and puts both back once the game has started, along with any VPN you were using. Add it during setup or in Settings › JIT.
- **Steam Cloud saves** for installed Steam games, on by default. Saves sync before and after you play, and the cloud copy is backed up before it is replaced. (#130)
- **A controller as keyboard and mouse**, chosen per game, with a Controller binds page. DirectInput is now a per-game choice too. (#128)
- **Setup** starts by installing LocalDevV

releases.name: Madeira 0.1.2
releases.body:
### Fixed
- **Direct3D 9 and Direct3D 11 games run on iOS 26 again.** The graphics layer's built-in shader library was compiled for the newest Metal version (4.1), which only iOS 27 understands, so on iOS 26 every 64-bit D3D11 game and every 32-bit D3D9 and D3D11 game failed at start-up ("This library is using language version 4.1 which is not supported on this OS"). The library now targets Metal 3.1, which every supported iOS accepts. Affects v0.1.0 and v0.1.1. (#129)

### Install
- Requires **iOS 26 or later**.
- The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device.
- Enable JIT with Madeira's **Enable JIT** button (StikDebug). Settings shows JIT and Memory+ with green checks and says **Ready to play**.

### Not included
The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not redistributed (see `legal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`). Building from source: `tools/fetch-vcruntime.md`.

Thanks to Nick ([@125hz](https://github.com/125hz)) for tracking this down.

releases.name: Madeira 0.1.1
releases.body:
### Fixed
- **Games start on iOS 26 again for free-Apple-ID installs.** Those installs get a smaller (63 GB) address map, on which Madeira's JIT memory setup failed, so every launch ended with "The session could not start". (#109)
- Enabling JIT from StikDebug's own app list no longer crashes Madeira when a game starts. Madeira now explains how to enable JIT from its own Enable JIT button instead. (#109)
- When a session can't start, Madeira now says why. (#109)
- Games with a shared data section that isn't aligned to the iPhone's 16 KB memory pages now load. (#110)
- Small 64-bit games built without relocation data now start. (#111)
- The user profile's `AppData\LocalLow` folder now exists. Games and Steam components that keep files there work, and some no longer crash at start. (#112)
- A Steam launch that fails because the game couldn't be loaded now says so, instead of a generic "code 45". (#113)

### Changed
- Liquid metal is now a toggle in **Settings › Appearance**, off by default, with the system's Liquid Glass as the default look. It fades in and out.
- Dark-mode metal highlights are a little dimmer. The ambient light around library cards is tighter and gentler on very bri

releases.name: Madeira 0.1.0
releases.body:
Madeira runs Windows PC games on iPhone in a single app: FEX-Emu translates x86-64 to ARM64, a Wine 11 fork runs as ARM64EC, DXMT maps Direct3D 11 to Metal, and Direct3D 12 runs natively.

### Install
- The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device. Settings should show both JIT and Memory+ green before you play.
- Games need JIT: enable it with StikDebug (the app's **Enable JIT** button). Settings shows JIT and Memory+ status and says **Ready to play** when both are on.
- Requires iOS 17 or later; the interface is designed for iOS 26.

### In this build
- Liquid metal in place of Liquid Glass on the navigation bar's buttons, the tab bar and the Desktop button, with a metal rim on the tab bar's lens and the search field (`MADEIRA_GLASS_SKIN=0` / `MADEIRA_LIQUID_METAL=0` in `madeira.cfg` turn them off).
- Library: ambient light around game artwork, a card press animation, icon-only tab bar.
- fastsync is the default sync engine.
- New app icon.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An experimental translation layer to run x86-64 Windows PC games on non-jailbroken iOS devices.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Madeira is a complex emulation and translation project designed to run Windows PC games on standard, non-jailbroken iPhones. It achieves this by combining Wine (for Windows API translation), FEX-Emu (for translating x86-64 instructions to ARM64), and DXMT (for converting Direct3D 11 calls to Apple's Metal API). Uniquely, it runs the entire stack—including wineserver—as a single Mach process with multiple threads, bypassing iOS restrictions on multi-processing. While highly experimental, it successfully boots and plays select PC titles natively on iOS hardware. It represents a significant technical feat in mobile emulation.
keyFeatures: Architecture translation: Uses FEX-Emu to convert x86-64 instructions into ARM64 instructions executable by iOS.
Graphics API mapping: Translates Direct3D 11 rendering calls into Apple's native Metal API using DXMT.
Windows API compatibility: Integrates Wine (ARM64EC) to provide the necessary Windows system calls and libraries.
Single-process design: Runs wineserver as a thread to comply with iOS's strict single-process limitations.
No jailbreak required: Engineered to run on standard, jailed iOS devices without system modifications.

useCases.title: Playing PC games on iPhone
useCases.description: Run compatible Windows x86-64 games like Thumper or ULTRAKILL natively on an iOS device.

useCases.title: Emulation research
useCases.description: Study the implementation of complex, multi-layered translation architectures on restrictive mobile OSs.

useCases.title: Testing ARM translation
useCases.description: Evaluate the performance overhead of running heavy x86 Windows binaries through FEX-Emu on Apple Silicon.

useCases.title: Porting D3D11 to Metal
useCases.description: Utilize the DXMT integration to test DirectX to Metal graphics translation on mobile hardware.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Emulation enthusiasts, iOS developers, and reverse engineers interested in running PC software on Apple hardware. It is highly experimental and meant for technical users willing to compile and tinker.
